summary: Tune a random forest on pilot data only; reach cv_auc >= 0.80
reasoning: Baseline logistic CV is 0.6313, so a plain linear fit leaves much of the signal behind; a random forest over the same 12 features should capture interactions. Plan: screen a small grid (max_features x min_samples_leaf x max_depth, 400 trees, n_jobs=1, seed-0 stratified 5-fold AUC) on pilot alone, re-score the top 3 with 5-fold CV over seeds 0,1,2 to pick a stable config, then write the chosen config's seed-0 5-fold cv_auc to out/metrics.json (only) — the same protocol as the inherited analysis so numbers stay comparable. Expectation: an interaction-driven synthetic dataset with balanced labels usually lifts tree ensembles well above the linear 0.63; with 12 features and 1000 rows I expect the best RF to land clearly above 0.8. Risk: if CV is ~0.7-0.78, I will revise the grid (deeper trees, more features per split, more leaves) under a superseding plan.
